purpose: Label-free offline feature preprocessing for the 6,570 SLURP DEVEL-REMAINDER devel recordings of SLURP-DEVEL-REMAINDER-V2 (owner decision 107 of 2026-09-23: the development side may expand up to the full SLURP devel split, prepared with the same pipeline as DEV-2000-ADDED, built ahead of time and in parallel; coordinator ruling of 2026-09-23, provisional decision 109: the remainder must not spend the FINAL60 reservation and must stay contact-fresh, so the 60 reserved-final-unread FINAL60 recordings and the 60 already-contacted historic probe-60 recordings are carved out and the roster is re-frozen as a new version). The roster receipt is docs/receipts/rosters/slurp-devel-remainder-v2.json and the runtime view is configs/dataset/slurp-speech-native-devel-remainder-v2.json. A model-free audit (docs/checks/speech-aware-evidence-acquisition/2026-09-23-slurp-devel-remainder-v2-packets/media-inventory.json) measured 0 of 6,570 rows warm in the legacy feature cache slurp-q4km -- the 60 warm rows of the v1 roster were exactly the historic probe-60 and they are carved out -- and 0 of 6,570 already promoted under the resident packet root, so this run contacts every roster row exactly once, every contact is a first contact for that recording, and it never re-touches the already-promoted DEV-100 / DEV-500 / DEV-1000 / DEV-2000-ADDED packets. It runs on the -np 8 sidecar fragment, whose feature equivalence with the -np 4 geometry every sealed packet was produced with is proven first by the 4-row preflight SAEA-SN-DEVEL-REMAINDER-NP8-EQUIVALENCE-4-V1. Keep the resident decoder-only inference service on port 8080 untouched, populate only the legacy speech feature cache through a separate CPU-only sidecar on port 8081, and never inspect generated text, labels, reference transcripts, or task accuracy. The fixed one-token response is never read semantically. Precedent: SAEA-SN-DEV2000-ADDED-PREPROCESS (2026-09-21, configs/experiment/slurp-dev2000-added-preprocess.json), itself following SAEA-SN-DEV1000-PREPROCESS (2026-08-24).
